rows: Quarter-size hail reported at Sipe Springs.
60 MPH wind gust measured in town.
Power lines down in the Hasse area.
Hail ranging in size from nickels to half-dollars fell in a large swath near the intersection of CR 413 and Highway 16. The amount of hail created hail fog. Several cars were damaged.
A number of barns and sheds had roofs ripped off in the Edna Hill area.
Reported on FM 2382 in the southeastern part of the county.
Complete roof loss on a building in downtown. Also a metal shed on Highway 6 was destroyed.

Estimated winds of 65 mph were reported in Newburg.

Penny size hail fell in DeLeon.
Large trees in DeLeon were snapped at their bases or knocked down.
Golfball size hail was reported in Downing.
A trained spotter reported Golfball size hail 1 mile west of Comanche.
Large oak trees were snapped approximately 2/3 of the way up and an outbuilding was blown away.
Golfball size hail was reported 8 miles southwest of Comanche.
Nickel size hail was reported in Comanche.
Part of the metal roofing of the White Point Community Center was peeled back.
A large live oak tree with a base diameter of several feet was uprooted and blown onto a house on CR 251.
Golfball size hail was reported 1 mile south of Newburg.
Golfball size hail was reported 1 mile west of the city of Comanche.
Penny size hail fell 5 miles west of Carlton.
A tree fell on FM 1496 approximately 3 miles north of Proctor.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Highway 36 and FM 589 northwest of Comanche.
A wind gust was estimated to be 60 mph. Dime size hail was also reported.
Penny size hail fell in the town of Proctor.
Damaging downburst winds hit a home 2 miles outside the city of Comanche, ripping off most of the roof and uprooting a large mulberry tree. The tree fell across the garage.
Trees and tree limbs of various sizes were blown down by thunderstorm winds.
Nickel sized hail was reported west of DeLeon.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported 8 miles northwest of Comanche.
Quarter sized hail was reported 17 miles northwest of Comanche.
One and a quarter inch hail fell 4 miles west of DeLeon.
A brief EF-0 tornado occurred with no damage approximately 2 miles north-northwest of Sidney.

Severe thunderstorm winds, likely from the RFD of a supercell, caused damage about a mile east of DeLeon along Highway 6. Tree limbs were snapped, the metal roof of a building was partially peeled back, and light poles at a baseball field were snapped or knocked down.
Baseball size hail fell just west of the town of Beattie.
Golfball to baseball size hail fell just west of Sidney.
Golfball sized hail was reported at the intersection of County Road 416 and Farm-to-Market Road 2861 about 5 miles northeast of Comanche.
Golfball size hail fell in the town of Carlton.
Thunderstorm winds blew down large tree limbs in Gustine, which is approximately 10 miles east of Comanche.
Several large trees were blown over around the city of De Leon.
A 60 MPH wind gust was reported northwest of De Leon.
A 60 MPH wind gust was reported east of De Leon.
Nickel-sized hail was reported 3 miles south of Gorman.

A 64 mph wind gust was measured at the automated weather station at Comanche County airport (KMKN). The sheriff's office reported large tree limbs and power lines were knocked down around the city of Comanche.
A 69 MPH wind gust was measure at the Comanche County Airport (KMKN).
Comanche Fire Department reported dime sized hail covering the ground.
Amateur radio operators reported golf ball sized hail approximately 5 miles south of Deleon.
Golf ball sized hail was reported in Downing.
Penny sized hail was reported along Highway 377 near Proctor.
The Comanche County Emergency Manager reported golf ball sized hail at Lake Proctor.
Amateur radio operators reported the hail grew to the size of Quarters in Proctor.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Duster which is west-northwest of DeLeon.
Quarter sized hail was reported 10 miles west of DeLeon.
Quarter sized hail was reported at Lake Proctor.
Half dollar sized hail was covering the ground in Proctor.
Golf ball sized hail was reported in Sidney.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Comanche.
Comanche County Volunteer Fire Departments reported golf ball sized hail near the community of Rucker.
Comanche County Volunteer Fire Departments reported golf ball sized hail that was covering the ground near DeLeon.
The Comanche County Sheriff's Office reported a roof blown off of a building in Comanche. This same storm damaged several transformers, power lines and significant tree damage.
Tree limbs of 3-6 inches were knocked down in DeLeon.
Strong thunderstorm winds blew down trees in and around De Leon. Winds were estimated at 70-80 mph.
Amateur radio operators and storm chasers observed a tornado in the far northwestern corner of Comanche County. This tornado occurred over ranch land and caused little damage.

Amateur radio operators and storm chasers observed a second tornado to the northwest of Sidney. This tornado also occurred over ranch land and caused minimal damage, this time much closer to the city of Sidney.
Softball sized hail smashed at least one windshield in Duster.
Baseball sized hail was reported 7 miles west of De Leon; near Duster.
Trained spotters observed a tornado to the north of the city of Proctor, on the northeast side of Proctor Lake. Several trees were damaged, but no structures suffered damage.

Amateur radio operators and trained spotters observed a tornado, originally reported to be twelve miles north of Gustine. The tornado damage was noted by local emergency management to be just north of U.S. 377, on the northeast side of the city of Proctor. While the tornado occur…
Golf ball sized hail was 2 inches deep on Highway 6 at the Comanche/Erath County line.
A 60 mph wind gust was estimated 2 miles north of Proctor.
Amateur radio operators reported golf ball sized hail between Comanche and DeLeon, on State Highway 16.
The Comanche County emergency manager reported golf ball sized hail fell along County Road 590 approximately five miles southwest of the city of Comanche.
A 62 MPH wind gust was measured at Comanche County Airport.
Amateur radio reported a 60 MPH wind gust approximately 1 mile northwest of Comanche, TX.
A 70 MPH wind gust was measured at the Comanche, TX Remote Automated Weather Station.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down in Sidney by strong thunderstorm winds. Trees were also knocked down to the east of Sidney at the intersection of CR 157 and CR 103.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a house roof a half mile south of Sidney.
Comanche County Sheriff's Department reported quarter sized hail in the city of Comanche.
An MPING report indicated quarter-sized hail approximately 8 miles east-northeast of the city of Comanche, TX.
Baseball and softball size hail 4 miles north of De Leon.
RAWS site COAT2 reported a wind gust of 62 mph.
Baseball size hail reported 1 mile SSW of Comanche.

A social media report indicated quarter size hail in the city of De Leon, TX.
A public report indicated quarter size hail in the city of De Leon, TX.
Large tree branches were broken off a property on CR 110 in the northwest portions of Comanche County.
An attached garage collapsed from thunderstorm winds. A car and other contents of the garage were damaged. This damage was located along TX 16 about 5 miles north of the City of Comanche.
Large tree branches were broken on the west side of Lake Proctor.
Dime to quarter size hail was reported.
The metal siding and roof of a large barn was partially torn off.
Tree damage was reported in and around Comanche. Some business signs and carports were also damaged.
Tree and shed damage was reported around Proctor Lake.

Broadcast media reported tennis ball sized hail along Highway 16 north of Comanche.
Minor damage to the press box and concession building at Comanche High School Football Stadium.
The Comanche County-City Airport AWOS measured 50 kts of wind.
Reported via mPING south of Dublin.

The Automated Weather Observation System at Comanche Airport measured a wind gust of 58 MPH.
